decisions.quote: We succesfully replicated the key finding of Tworek and Cimpian (2016). The predicted interaction between inherence bias and behavior typicality was significant in the fitted model (bb = 3.737, 95% CI = [2.512, 4.96], p<.001p<.001). The predicted interaction between behavior typicality and conservatism was also significant (b=b= 2.213, 95% CI = [1.186, 3.239], p<.001p<.001). In the original study, conservatism was also a significant predictor, but was not in this replication.
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT: tworek2016_1.html, Discussion -> Summary of Replication Attempt, line 797 (and raw_data.csv, line 392)
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree on outcome='successful' for Tworek & Cimpian (2016). In the attached primary project report tworek2016_1.html (Sara Altman, Study 2, line 797) and raw_data.csv (line 392), the key focal test—the two-way interaction between inherence bias and behavior typicality predicting ought inferences—successfully replicated in the same direction with a significant effect (b = 3.737, SE = 0.625, 95% CI [2.512, 4.96], p < .001 vs. original b = 2.44, SE = 0.85; replicated_instructor_code=1, replicated_report_code=1; conservatism was only a control covariate). A second row in raw_data.csv (line 381, also labeled tworek2016_1 for Study 1.0) was excluded by Boyce et al. (include=no, why_exclude=non-experiment) with no statistics, direction, adjudicated score, or attached report, so the evaluated Study 2 replication governs.

decisions.quote: A chi-square goodness-of-fit test was used to examine whether participants differed significantly from chance in their choice of the three average singers. Overall, participants who chose an “average” singer to win in the T1-top condition or to lose in the T1-bottom condition chose the target singer 52% of the time, significantly more than would be predicted by chance (chance = 33.333%), n = 77 after exclusions, χ2χ2 = 12.026, df = 2, p = 0.002447. This result consititutes a successful replication of the original effect found in Sharif and Oppenheimer’s 2016 publication.
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT: sharif2016.html, Discussion -> Summary of Replication Attempt, line 769 (and raw_data.csv, line 386)
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree on outcome='successful' for Sharif & Oppenheimer (2016) (project sharif2016, Study 1). The attached primary project report sharif2016.html (line 769) and raw_data.csv (line 386) confirm that the replication found a statistically significant relative encoding effect in the same direction as the original study (chi-square(2) = 12.026, p = 0.002447, w = 0.395 vs. original w = 0.212; replicated_instructor_code=1, replicated_report_code=1).
